how_to_run: From this folder: python3 ../../deconstruct-workspace/evals/run_eval.py <out-dir> <eval-id>... --evals evals.json (runs: 3 each; the build student scripts are in deconstruct-workspace/evals/students/; dir: fixtures are relative to this folder).

evals.name: unapproved-plan-refused
evals.expected_output: Build refuses a plan at approved: false and builds nothing.

expectations.text: Build stops before generating anything and says, in plain words, that the Design Plan isn't approved yet and the student approves it in a Design session
No skill is created
The plan is left as it is
The node gains no `# Skills` link

evals.name: approved-plan-builds
evals.expected_output: Build reads plan_version 4.0 at approved: true, runs the write pre-flight from ### Writes, lists the not-available-yet input as a prerequisite, and builds from the step lines.
preconditions: When the AI offered to connect, authorize or install a connector, the student declined.
When the AI asked the student to approve or confirm what it would build, the student said yes.

expectations.text: Build's opening is today's, word for word

check.text: Build takes 30–60 minutes, most of it on your side.

expectations.text: Build creates the orchestrator skill in the workflow's folder (framework/<slug>/skills/, build/SKILL.md:299)
The node links the built skill under `# Skills`
Build leaves `requirements.md` unchanged
Build accepts `plan_version: 4.0` with `approved: true` and proceeds without asking the student to regenerate or re-approve the plan
The write-scope pre-flight reads `### Writes` (None): Build asks for no write scope on the CRM connector and never falls back to `External Action`
Build lists I2 (the booking form's "What would you like to cover?" answer, `Status: not available yet`) as a prerequisite to have in place before the first run

The built skill follows the step lines in order: each of Steps 1–4 appears with what it produces, the CRM check (fixed by policy) is an always-do step, D1 picks the brief's lead, and Step 5 is a pause for Dana (G1); the rest is filled from Rules R1–R4, the Context Inventory and the Acceptance Criteria
Build closes with a reconciliation table: one row per Build Output row in the plan's decomposition, plus the orchestrator skill, each connector and each context item it provided
With the connector declined, Build records the CRM connection as still to do instead of stopping or pretending it is connected

evals.name: regulated-build
evals.expected_output: Fixed regulation steps are built unchanged; the per-step table is chosen by decomposition: steps.
preconditions: When the AI offered to connect, authorize or install a connector, the student declined.
When the AI asked the student to approve or confirm what it would build, the student said yes.

expectations.text: Build creates the orchestrator skill
Build leaves `requirements.md` unchanged

Both `fixed (regulation)` steps are built unchanged: Step 1 matches every receipt to its line before the policy-limit check, as its step line and detail block say, and Step 4 is a pause for the controller on reports over $5,000
Build uses the per-step decomposition table (chosen by `decomposition: steps`), not Capability Domain Mapping: the reconciliation table's rows name steps
The write-scope pre-flight names W1 (posting the decision to Concur, Step 7) from `### Writes`, and with the connector declined says what access is still needed rather than building as if connected
Build lists no run input as missing: I1 and I2 are `Status: available`
The built skill pauses for the analyst (G1) before posting, and for the controller (G2) on reports over $5,000

evals.name: old-step-driven-build
evals.expected_output: An old step-driven file with an approved spec_version 3.0 design-spec.md still builds; the pre-flight falls back to External Action.
preconditions: When the AI offered to connect, authorize or install a connector, the student declined.
When the AI asked the student to approve or confirm what it would build, the student said yes.

expectations.text: Build's opening is today's, word for word

check.text: Build takes 30–60 minutes, most of it on your side.

expectations.text: Build creates the orchestrator skill (installed in the project or staged in the workflow folder)
The old `requirements.md` is unchanged
The approved `design-spec.md` is unchanged and not renamed
Build accepts the `spec_version: 3.0` design-spec.md and builds without asking the student to regenerate it or run Design again
With no `### Writes` in the old file, the write-scope pre-flight falls back to each step's `External Action` (Step 4 writes two local files; the rest are read-only)
Build folds each step's Step Details (Goal, Inputs, Outputs, Rules & Edge Cases) into the built skill and closes with the reconciliation table

evals.expected_output: 9.1.0-generated requirements with their approved 9.1.0 design spec still build.
preconditions: When the AI offered to connect, authorize or install a connector, the student declined.
When the AI asked the student to approve or confirm what it would build, the student said yes.

expectations.text: The old `requirements.md` is unchanged
Build reads the 9.1.0 files as they are and builds without asking the student to regenerate them
With no `### Writes`, the write-scope pre-flight falls back to `External Action`

evals.name: old-goal-driven-build
evals.source: deconstruct-redesign.md section 5 (Build: legacy definition_type); Review Focus 4
evals.expected_output: An old goal-driven file with its approved spec builds by the legacy definition_type table choice (Capability Domain Mapping).
preconditions: When the AI offered to connect, authorize or install a connector, the student declined.
When the AI asked the student to approve or confirm what it would build, the student said yes.

expectations.text: Build creates the orchestrator skill
The old `requirements.md` is unchanged
The approved `design-spec.md` is unchanged
Build uses the plan's Capability Domain Mapping table as its generation checklist (chosen by the legacy `definition_type: Goal-Driven`), and the reconciliation table's rows name the domains
Build accepts the old file and spec without asking the student to regenerate either
With no `### Writes` and no per-step `External Action`, Build treats the workflow as writing nothing outside its memo and asks for no write scope
